title_clean: The 0 Risk Investment Through Options Strategy (Muhurat Investment)
summary: Long-term bullish combo revealed: 10 lots Nifty Dec-2022 futures long @17,200 hedged by next-Dec 17,000 put bought @1,410, premium funded by selling 1,500 qty 21,000 calls @~455. MTM +8L future, -5L put, +22K calls; rolls futures into Jan-Feb until Dec-2023.
lessons: A far-dated put can be fully funded by selling far-OTM calls, turning a leveraged long into a near-zero-premium protected bet.
Roll futures monthly; keep the hedge structure intact across series.
Nov-Feb is the prime window for long-term options positions.
Admit the hedge bleeds (put -5L vs future +8L) and offset it with short puts lower down rather than dismantling the structure.

title_clean: The World's Best Trader Goes Bankrupt - What About Us
summary: Three real ruin stories against MTM-screenshot culture: Jesse Livermore's bankruptcy and suicide; a villager who borrowed from his village at 6%/month to ride the 2008-11 gold bull on 5% margin and was wiped out by one 10% overnight gold crash, then jailed; Nick Leeson and Barings (Kobe earthquake gap down, bank sold for £1).
lessons: Only bring to the market what you can afford to lose entirely.
5% commodity margin means a 10% adverse move can wipe 200% of capital in one session.
A full year of posted profits proves nothing about future survival; risk is risk.
Investors taking delivery can survive any fall; leveraged traders with expiry deadlines cannot.
Verify capital, backup and lifestyle before following any trader's screenshots.

summary: Derives the 2023 Nifty target of 21,000: 15-year candle study shows down years are followed by green years; US century statistics (down year -> next year ~+15%, only 4/100 double-downs); four live problems (US inflation peaking, European gas -65% off peak, China reopening, FII selling ~3L crore) all seen as resolving; VIX 15 implies a 15% move to ~20,700-21,000.
lessons: Historically, a down year for Indian or US markets is followed by an up year; back-to-back down years are rare (~4%).
A VIX of 15 means the market prices a ~15% move - use implied move, not gut feel, for annual ranges.
Implied volatility exceeds realized volatility, so straddle premiums offer less than the full implied move.
FII selling of ~1 billion dollars/week no longer crashes the market because retail + mutual funds absorb it.
FIIs eventually face FOMO after long selling - their capitulation can ignite the next leg up.

title_clean: 2 Events That Can Destroy Indian Markets in 2023
summary: Two 2023 risks: (1) LTCG tinkering - removal but taxation at slab (~35%) or 3-year holding period would be worse for markets than 2018's 10% reintroduction, with the FII treaty problem (FPIs pay no Indian tax on F&O business income under DTAA, so the exchequer could lose); (2) inheritance/estate-tax mechanics - would force asset sales and push wealth into company structures, formalizing the economy.
lessons: Removing a tax can be worse than keeping it if the replacement taxes harder - read the mechanism, not the headline.
DTAA lets many FPIs trade Indian F&O as business income without Indian tax; changing that changes FII behavior.
An inheritance tax forces heirs to sell assets to pay the bill, creating forced-supply waves.
High personal tax vs low corporate tax pushes wealth into company structures, formalizing the economy.
India-specific: without social security, wealth-transfer taxes hit hardest and are politically explosive.
